findings.title: New installations bypass GitHub-user validation
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist the code returns pipeline.next_step() without comparing pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to the installer. The sender check on lines 501-505 only runs when an Integration row already exists. Since the Integration row is created asynchronously by the GitHub webhook, an attacker can complete the pipeline before the webhook creates the row, or when the webhook is delayed/failed, and link an arbitrary installation_id without proving they installed the GitHub App. The existing tests prove this: assert_setup_flow creates an integration with no webhook/sender and succeeds.

findings.title: Unhandled KeyError on missing integration sender metadata
findings.body: The check does integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with direct indexing. Metadata is not guaranteed to contain sender: build_integration only sets metadata["sender"] if state.get("sender"), and the pipeline only ever binds installation_id and github_authenticated_user, so pipeline-created integrations have no sender. Pre-existing/old integrations also lack it. When an orphaned Integration exists with no OrganizationIntegration, a retry hits this line and raises KeyError, producing a 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html error page and breaking reinstall flows.

findings.title: OAuth token exchange and user lookup can raise 500
findings.body: OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen for the access_token exchange and get_user_info for /user with no try/except. Network errors, non-2xx from GitHub, or an invalid/expired code/token will raise instead of returning a payload without access_token/login. Only missing keys in the parsed payload are handled. The consequence is a 500 on exactly the failure cases the PR description says should show the friendly Invalid installation request page.

findings.title: Pipeline state poisoned before OAuth state validation
findings.body: OAuthLoginView binds request.GET installation_id into pipeline state before checking if request.GET state equals pipeline.signature. A request with an invalid/forged state still mutates the stored installation_id before error() is returned. A subsequent legitimate retry that relies on pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id") will then use the attacker-controlled value, allowing fixation of the installation that will later be compared or built.

findings.title: Empty installation_id bypasses App redirect
findings.body: GitHubInstallation checks if installation_id is None, not if it is falsy. A request like ?installation_id= yields empty string, skips the redirect to the GitHub App URL, does Integration.objects.get(external_id="") and on DoesNotExist calls pipeline.next_step(). This proceeds to build_integration with an empty ID and a needless GitHub API call, instead of redirecting to install the App.

findings.title: installation_not_found test no longer exercises 404
findings.body: test_installation_not_found now sends state ddd023... which does not match the expected pipeline signature 9cae5e..., so OAuthLoginView rejects with Invalid installation request before GitHubInstallation/build_integration ever calls GET /app/installations. The stubbed 404 is never hit and the assertion was changed from The GitHub installation could not be found. The 404 handling in build_integration is therefore untested.
